post.description:

schema.title: Response Load Analysis Rack Solve Api Load Analysis Rack Solve Post

post.description:
Slip gain |α_wheel/δ| and implied saturation steer δ_sat vs speed.

For a single steered wheel the steady-state bicycle solve gives the body
(β, r), hence α_wheel = β + r·x/V − δ. The gain grows ~(1 + mV²/(8CαL)),
so the linear region (δ_sat = α_peak/gain) shrinks with speed — exactly the
high-speed behaviour the load page exposes.

schema.title: Response Bicycle Gain Api Model Demo Bicycle Gain Post

post.description:
Pacejka Fy(α) at a chosen vertical load — the real ``pacejka_combined_forces``.

Cornering stiffness is the load-sensitive value at this Fz, so the small-slip
slope and the μ·Fz peak both move with load just like the foundation model.

schema.title: Response Tire Curve Api Model Demo Tire Curve Post

post.description:
τ_kingpin split into Fy / Fx / Mz / KPI terms vs δ for one wheel.

Reuses ``sweep_load_analysis`` to produce the *real* per-δ tyre forces
(Fx, Fy, Mz, Fz) — exactly what the load page shows — then decomposes the
kingpin moment with ``kingpin_torque_terms`` (the same helper ``kingpin_torque``
sums). No physics is duplicated.

BatchRequest.title: BatchRequest
BatchRequest.description: Either a stored experiment name or an inline definition, plus variants.

CompareSpec.title: CompareSpec
CompareSpec.description: Cross-run aggregation: how to group the grid and what to measure against.

Criterion.title: Criterion
Criterion.description:
A falsifiable claim about the result.

`must` is a small comparison language rather than a Python expression on
purpose: a criterion that can run arbitrary code is a criterion nobody can
review at a glance.

`at` selects which cells must satisfy it — "all", or an equality filter on
sweep coordinates such as "speed_kmh == 140".

DisturbanceCreate.title: DisturbanceCreate
DisturbanceCreate.description:
Type-tagged disturbance creation. Bounds keep the sim numerically safe
(e.g. stiffness cap prevents the Fz-pulse blowup fixed in Phase 3).

DisturbanceUpdate.title: DisturbanceUpdate
DisturbanceUpdate.description: Partial update — same bounds as create, everything optional.

ExprMetric.title: ExprMetric
ExprMetric.description:
A derived metric written as an expression over a run's channels.

The safe tier: no statements, no imports, no attribute access — see
`metrics.py`. Anything this cannot express (correlation-based phase
estimation, injected-noise sensitivity) needs the plugin tier.

FaultSpec.title: FaultSpec
FaultSpec.description:
Target faults retain actuator dynamics; jam/free act on the mechanism.

stuck_hold locks the actuator coordinate; alignment/K&C still apply.
Sensor faults affect observations only, not controller feedback.

ManeuverStep.title: ManeuverStep
ManeuverStep.description: One segment of a maneuver, ending after `duration` sim-seconds.

ParamsUpdate.title: ParamsUpdate
ParamsUpdate.description:
Partial vehicle-parameter update. All fields optional; bounds reject
physically meaningless values (pydantic returns 422 with details).

PathSpec.title: PathSpec
PathSpec.description: Reference path for follow_trajectory: template or explicit waypoints.

RecordingStart.title: RecordingStart
RecordingStart.description: Optional channel selection. If omitted, current channels are kept.

SolveFor.title: SolveFor
SolveFor.description:
A sweep axis whose values are solved for rather than listed.

Declared in the schema from day one so specs written now stay valid, but
the runner refuses it until the solver phase lands — see
docs/agent_interface_design.md §4 for why this is harder than a bisection
(a_y is not monotone in steer angle past the friction peak).

SteerProfile.title: SteerProfile
SteerProfile.description:
Steering input as a function of time within one step.

`unit` selects how `amplitude` is interpreted:
  * "normalized" (default, legacy): [-1, 1], goes through the strategy's
    steering-feel mapping (variable gear ratio, soft limit).
  * "front_deg": front-wheel angle in degrees. The experiment applies this
    directly to delta_cmd, bypassing the feel layer — so a regression
    baseline survives future tuning of the driver-input mapping.

StudySpec.title: StudySpec
StudySpec.description: The complete declaration of one study.

SweepAxis.title: SweepAxis
SweepAxis.description:
One dimension of the grid.

`bind` is the dotted path into the baseline Experiment's JSON form that
this axis writes, exactly as `experiment/batch.py` expects.

anchor.title: Anchor
anchor.description: Named scenario anchor to place the course on
